name: Dutch Baby Pancake

instructions.primary_message: Bring the eggs to room temperature. Bring the whole milk to room temperature.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 large eggs
¾ cup whole milk

instructions.primary_message: For the Batter: In a blender, blend eggs, milk, flour, sugar, and salt until smooth, about 20 seconds. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours.
Adjust oven rack to middle position. Set a 30-cm cast-iron skillet on the rack, and preheat oven to 230°C (450°F). Remove batter from refrigerator while oven preheats.

When oven has preheated, remove skillet from oven, and add butter; using gloved hands or oven mitts, carefully swirl skillet to coat bottom and edges of pan with butter until completely melted, about 20 seconds. Pour batter into pan and bake for 10 minutes. With skillet still in oven, reduce oven temperature to 205°C (400°F) and bake until golden brown and significantly puffed around edges, 8 to 10 minutes more.

Meanwhile, for the Whipped Crème Fraîche: In a medium bowl, whisk crème fraîche, sugar, vanilla paste, and salt until medium-stiff peaks form, about 1 minute. Cover with a plate or plastic wrap, and refrigerate until ready to use. If mixture has loosened, briefly whisk again to medium-stiff peaks before serving.

To Serve: Remove Dutch baby from oven. Using a small fine-mesh sieve, dust pancake with confectioners' sugar, and serve with whipped crème fraîche, lemon wedges, and fresh berries, if desired. Serve immediately.

description: This Dutch baby has a custardy center and crispy edges, and it comes together with minimal effort—perfect for an easy yet impressive brunch.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 45 min.

Optional or for serving: Lemon wedges, for serving; Fresh blueberries and raspberries, optional

Notes: Vanilla extract can be substituted for the paste in equal amounts, but its flavor won’t be quite as robust.

Make-ahead and storage: The Dutch baby is best eaten immediately after it's baked.
author: Laila Ibrahim
